lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Andre! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the bedtime goal went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than I thought. 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your phone in the bedroom at night?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you watch TV in bed?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Work took over this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can turn off the TV at 10:30. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. Between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd do it if the day had a few more hours.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have more energy when I go to bed earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the bedtime goal going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the bedtime goal. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to be in bed by 10 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 9. Maybe 10.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

flags.reason: Repeats the phone-out-of-bedroom information verbatim after participant already responded; ignores client's reply and pushes advice.
Asks whether 5 days is realistic, a coach-set target, instead of exploring the participant's own goal first.
Praises follow-through before participant showed it; affirmation not grounded in what was said.

score.summary: The coach reviewed the bedtime goal, elicited a specific 4-night target with high confidence, and used several useful reflections, especially around the participant's diabetes and cancer-recurrence motivation. Early closed questions, a repeated information statement at line 37, and a coach-set 5-day target reduced partnership.
strengths: Line 36: 'Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.' supports autonomy.
Line 41 and 43: complex reflections capture the participant's sense that this is necessary and about getting life back.
Line 49: open question led the participant to set their own goal of 4 nights.
coaching_tips: Line 37 repeats line 34 right after the participant responded; instead, ask permission or reflect the participant's reply in line 38.
Line 14 introduces a 5-day target the participant had not raised; start with an open question about what feels doable.
Line 11 praises follow-through before the participant showed it; wait for evidence before affirming.
Line 8 and 20 are closed questions; open questions such as line 6 work better to explore barriers.
Close with a summary and a concrete next contact date; neither occurred.
